raw_case_text:
A 53-year-old morbidly obese female with a history of hypertension presented to the emergency department (ED), with a sudden onset of loss of consciousness, left-sided weakness, and altered sensorium for two days, which was associated with high-grade fever and vomiting. At admission, she was unconscious (Glasgow coma scale, or GCS, score = 5); had tachypnea (respiratory rate, or RR, 30-35 minute-1), tachycardia (heart rate, or HR, 114 bpm), and blood pressure (BP) 153/90 mmHg; was maintaining oxygen saturation of 94% to 94% (on room air) on spontaneous respiration; and was passing urine output around 40-50 mL/hour. Given airway protection, tracheal intubation was performed immediately. Post intubation, the GCS was 6. Noncontrast computerized tomography (NCCT) of the brain revealed right basal ganglia bleeding with intraventricular hemorrhage (Figure 1).
Then she was transferred to ICU, where cerebral protection strategy (head-up position, neck in a neutral position, osmotic diuretics, mean arterial pressure (MAP) 85-90 mm Hg, normoxia, normocarbia, euglycemia, normothermia, and maintenance of sodium (Na+) levels between 145 and 155 mEq/L) and further supportive care was initiated. Laboratory evaluation at admission is summarized in Table 1. Electrocardiography (ECG) showed sinus tachycardia. Chest X-ray (CXR) was normal.   
After a few days of ICU admission, she started spiking high-grade temperature (core temperature as high as 106-107  F), which was associated with rhabdomyolysis (serum creatine kinase (CK-total) = 10,000 IU/L), stage III acute kidney injury (AKI, requiring five sessions of renal replacement therapy), and coagulopathy (requiring blood component therapy). On workup, cultures turned out to be sterile. Other possibilities of hyperthermia (such as drug toxicity) were ruled out. NCCT head was repeated, which did not reveal any hematoma expansion. Workup for COVID-19 was also negative. On account of a history of fever with chill and myalgia around a week before ED admission, a tropical workup was sent for malaria, typhoid, leptospirosis, dengue, chikungunya, and scrub typhus, in which serology (IgM antibodies) for dengue turned out to be positive. Gradually, the temperature trends, renal functions, and coagulopathy recovered. In intercurrent issues, she had septic shock (secondary to ventilator-associated pneumonia and grade IV pressure injury in the sacral region) and neuromuscular weakness, resulting in prolonged weaning. Eventually, the patient was discharged after six months of ICU stay in tracheostomized condition, with a GCS score of 9, accepting Ryle's tube feeding and passing adequate urine output.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 53-year-old female presenting with sudden loss of consciousness, left-sided hemiparesis, and altered sensorium for two days, associated with high-grade fever and vomiting.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 53-year-old female with a history of fever, chills, and myalgias one week prior presented with acute-onset loss of consciousness, left-sided weakness, altered sensorium, high fever, and vomiting lasting 2 days. On ED presentation, she was comatose (GCS 5) and in severe respiratory distress, requiring immediate endotracheal intubation. Following transfer to the ICU, she developed extreme hyperpyrexia (temperatures 106-107 °F), massive rhabdomyolysis, stage III acute kidney injury requiring hemodialysis, coagulopathy, and secondary septic shock.
subjective.past_medical_history: Hypertension; morbid obesity. History of fever with chills and myalgia one week before admission.
subjective.review_of_systems: Vomiting, high-grade fever, left hemiparesis, loss of consciousness.

objective.physical_examination: Emergency Department: Unconscious (GCS 5, post-intubation GCS 6). Respiratory rate 30-35 breaths/min (tachypnea), heart rate 114 bpm (tachycardia), blood pressure 153/90 mmHg, SpO2 94% on room air, urine output 40-50 mL/h. Neurological: Comatose, left hemiparesis. ICU course: Extreme hyperpyrexia with core temperatures reaching 106-107 °F; grade IV sacral pressure injury; severe critical illness neuromuscular weakness.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission: Sinus tachycardia on ECG; chest radiograph normal. ICU course: Serum total creatine kinase (CK) 10,000 IU/L (severe rhabdomyolysis); stage III acute kidney injury requiring five sessions of renal replacement therapy; coagulopathy requiring blood component therapy. Diagnostic workup: Blood, urine, and sputum cultures sterile; drug-induced hyperthermia excluded; COVID-19 PCR negative. Tropical febrile panel: Malaria, typhoid, leptospirosis, chikungunya, and scrub typhus negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Brain Non-contrast CT (admission): Acute right basal ganglia hemorrhage with intraventricular hemorrhage. Repeat Brain CT: Stable hematoma without enlargement.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Confirmed Dengue virus infection complicated by spontaneous hypertensive right basal ganglia hemorrhage with intraventricular extension, severe hyperpyrexia (core temperature 106-107 °F), severe rhabdomyolysis (CK 10,000 IU/L), stage III acute kidney injury, coagulopathy, ventilator-associated pneumonia, and critical illness polymyoneuropathy. Confirmed by positive Dengue IgM serology on tropical panel. Malaria, typhoid, leptospirosis, chikungunya, scrub typhus, COVID-19, and neuroleptic/drug toxicity were excluded.
Plan & Outcome: Emergency tracheal intubation and ICU transfer. Managed with targeted neuroprotective strategies (head elevation 30°, neutral neck position, osmotic diuresis, MAP 85-90 mmHg, normocapnia, targeted sodium 145-155 mEq/L), aggressive core cooling, blood component transfusions, and 5 sessions of renal replacement therapy / hemodialysis. Intercurrent septic shock from ventilator-associated pneumonia and grade IV sacral pressure ulcer treated with targeted antibiotics, wound care, and tracheostomy placement. Following six months of intensive ICU care, renal function and coagulopathy normalized, temperature resolved, and she was successfully discharged in a tracheostomized state (GCS 9) accepting enteral feeding.
